blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a model trained on a labelled source domain to an unlabelled target domain without access to the source data. Almost the entire SFDA literature assumes mutually exclusive classes, yet many deployed settings are multi-label. This paper formulates SFDA for multi-label classification and establishes the first benchmark for it: five adaptation tasks over six datasets spanning remote sensing, natural, clipart-style and driving imagery, with four single-label SFDA methods extended to provide the first baselines and a published multi-label method run alongside them, over three seeds. The benchmark shows that extending a single-label method is unreliable rather than merely suboptimal: half of the extended baselines fail to improve on the unadapted source model at all, and on two of the five tasks none of them does. The failures are not incidental. Nearest-centroid pseudo-labelling, softmax-based confidence, the diversity term of information maximization and confidence-weighted prototype construction each rely on mutual exclusivity, and each fails differently without it, so replacing the softmax with per-class sigmoids is a valid but insufficient extension. Multi-label Prototype Alignment with Contrastive Teaching (MPACT) is proposed in response, a mean-teacher framework whose objective, prototype construction and alignment term are each reconsidered for overlapping label sets. It attains the best average on every reported metric and is the only method that improves on the unadapted source model on all five tasks. The analysis further introduces a prototype-agreement diagnostic separating feature-space alignment from self-reinforcing agreement with the classifier, and reports a negative result for confidence-based pseudo-label filtering.
blocks.zh: 无源域适应(SFDA)将一个在被贴上标签的源域上训练的模型改用一个没有贴上标签的目标域而不访问源数据. 几乎所有SFDA文献都假定了相互排斥的类,然而许多被部署的设置都是多标签. 本文件为多标签分类制定了SFDA,并为它确定了第一个基准:在涵盖遥感、自然、剪接和驱动图像等6个数据集的基础上完成5个适应任务,扩展了4个单标签SFDA方法,以提供第一个基线,并公布了一个多标签方法。 基准显示,扩大单一标签方法是不可靠的,而不仅仅是次优化的:延长的基线有一半根本没有改进未经调整的源模型,而且五个任务中有两项没有改进。 失败不是偶然的。 近百分位机器人伪标签,软马克斯基于信心,信息最大化的多样性名词和信心加权原型构造各自依赖于相互排他性,没有这种名词,每个都不同地失败了,所以用每类相模取代软马克斯是有效但不充分的扩展. 作为回应,建议采用多标签原型校正与对照教学(MPACT),即一个平均教师框架,其目标、原型构建和校正术语都经过重新审议,以便使用重叠的标签。 它在每一个报告的衡量标准上都达到最佳平均值,是改进所有五项任务的未调整源模型的唯一方法。 分析还引入了原型-协议诊断法,将地物-空间配对与分类器的自强化协议区分开来,并报告了基于信任的伪标签过滤的负面结果.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The performance of deep classifiers drops when the distribution that
produced their test data differs from the distribution that produced their
training data ( Torralba and Efros, 2011 ) . Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) addresses this by
exploiting labeled source data and unlabeled target data ( Ganin and Lempitsky, 2015 ) , but the
assumption that source data remains available at adaptation time is often
not correct in practice: medical and satellite imagery is often licensed for a
single use, commercial datasets cannot be redistributed with a deployed model,
and online deployments rarely have enough storage or bandwidth to carry a large training
corpus. Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) removes that assumption, adapting
using only the pre-trained source model and unlabeled target data ( Liang et al., 2020 ) .

blocks.en:
SFDA research has developed rapidly, but almost the entire literature assumes single-label classification ( Liang et al., 2020 ; Cai et al., 2026 ) . This assumption is deeply embedded rather
than incidental. SHOT-style methods obtain pseudo-labels by assigning each
target sample to whichever class centroid lies closest to it ( Liang et al., 2020 ) ; information-maximization regularizers encourage
a near-uniform marginal over a set of mutually exclusive classes;
confidence measures are computed from a softmax distribution whose entries (i.e predictions for each class)
compete by construction. However, many of the settings practitioners actually face are
multi-label: an aerial image contains buildings , trees and pavement simultaneously; a driving scene contains car , person and traffic sign at once. A single-label SFDA method can be applied to such data by swapping the
softmax for per-class sigmoids, and that substitution is a valid extension. It
is not, however, a sufficient one: a method ported this way may fail to improve
on the unadapted source model, and can perform worse than leaving it
alone.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Multi-label UDA has received limited but growing attention. Approaches divide
into those that train a domain discriminator, such as DA-MAIC ( Lin et al., 2022 ) ,
and discriminator-free ones such as DALN ( Chen et al., 2022 ) and
DDA-MLIC ( Singh et al., 2026 ) .
DDA-MLIC derives its adversarial critic from the task classifier instead of an auxiliary subnet, with the reasoning that separating classification
from discrimination weakens both. Such
methods retain access to source data throughout adaptation and therefore serve
as a source-accessing reference rather than a comparable baseline, since the
setting studied here withholds source data entirely. This gap is reported
explicitly (Sections 6.1 and 7 ).

blocks.en:
Deprived of source data, SFDA methods must substitute some other signal
for the supervision they have lost, and they differ in what that signal
is. One family derives pseudo-labels from the structure of the target feature
space while regularizing the output distribution: SHOT ( Liang et al., 2020 ) freezes the source classifier, adapts only the feature extractor, and pairs
information maximization with pseudo-labels obtained from class centroids,
while AC-SFDA ( Cai et al., 2026 ) adds an adaptive curriculum over target samples. A
second family enforces agreement between each sample and its neighbours in
feature space ( Yang et al., 2021 ) . NVC-LLN ( Xu et al., 2025b ) belongs here, treating adaptation as learning with label noise. So does
UCON ( Xu et al., 2025a ) : its contrastive term attracts each sample to its nearest
neighbours and repels it from the rest of the batch, with an
augmentation-consistency term and a partial-label loss added to control the
uncertainty in that supervision. A third substitutes
self-supervision for the missing labels, typically a consistency or contrastive
objective over differently augmented views of the same target
image ( Karim et al., 2023 ) . A fourth
maintains a teacher as a temporal ensemble of the student and trains on its
denoised predictions ( Dasgupta et al., 2025 ) , the family to which the
framework proposed here belongs.
SHOT, UCON, NVC-LLN and AC-SFDA are the four methods extended and benchmarked in this paper.

blocks.en:
Two works address multi-label classification without source data.
NOTELA ( Boudiaf et al., 2023 ) augments a denoising teacher–student scheme with a
Laplacian term encouraging neighbouring points in feature space to receive
similar pseudo-labels, and evaluates it on multi-label bioacoustic recordings.
It reports that existing SFDA methods there can perform worse than no
adaptation at all, and that restricting the data to single-label recordings
recovers much of their performance – independent evidence, in another
modality, for the premise of this paper. Its own treatment of the multi-label
case is nonetheless the generic one, each class handled as an independent
binary problem, and its image benchmarks are single-label.
CoWA ( Jeong et al., 2026 ) adapts a multi-label chest X-ray classifier at test time,
weighting each sample by how far its predictions depart from the label
co-occurrence structure estimated from the target data; it updates only the
normalization parameters, in a single streaming pass. It addresses
test-time adaptation, in which the target data arrive as a stream and the model
is revised as they pass; the problem posed here is source-free domain
adaptation, in which the unlabelled target set is available in full and
offline. The two are neighbouring formulations but not the same, and a
method written for either carries assumptions the other does not make. The
setting studied here
differs from both: multi-label image classification, with the full unlabelled
target set available offline and the entire representation adapted over
multiple epochs.

blocks.en:
Two components of the framework proposed here are taken from the
single-label literature, not invented here: class prototypes and
a teacher–student pair. Class prototypes are widely used to structure a
target feature space: as
centroids for pseudo-labelling ( Liang et al., 2020 ) , as targets for
distribution alignment ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) , and as carriers of class information added
directly to target features to compensate for the domain shift ( Pan et al., 2025 ) . The Class Prototype Discovery construction of Zhou et al. (2024) is
the one adopted here.
The teacher–student scheme itself
originates outside domain adaptation, as a semi-supervised
method ( Tarvainen and Valpola, 2017 ) ; CleanAdapt-TS ( Dasgupta et al., 2025 ) shows for
source-free video action recognition that such a teacher yields more consistent
pseudo-labels than the source model alone, and AC-SFDA ( Cai et al., 2026 ) and
NOTELA ( Boudiaf et al., 2023 ) maintain one as well.

blocks.en:
Because target pseudo-labels are noisy by construction, losses that bound the
influence of a mislabelled example are directly relevant. The standard
approaches replace or temper the cross-entropy term: the mean absolute error is
robust to label noise but slow to converge, and generalized cross entropy
interpolates between the two ( Ghosh et al., 2017 ; Zhang and Sabuncu, 2018 ) ;
others reweight suspect samples rather than changing the
loss ( Shu et al., 2019 ) . Symmetric cross
entropy ( Wang et al., 2019 ) instead combines a
forward and a reverse term to bound the influence of mislabeled samples. Its binary, per-class analogue is used in the proposed framework (described in Section 4.1 ).

confidently mislabeled sample can contribute to the gradient. This is the

mean as much as towards the class. The weakness is therefore the same in both

displacements also differ in size from class to class, so the rarest classes,

blocks.en: 5.3 Extending single-label SFDA baselines

blocks.en:
To the best of our knowledge, no multi-label SFDA baseline exists for images. Of the two multi-label
source-free methods in Section 2 , NOTELA is evaluated on
bioacoustic recordings and its image benchmarks are single-label; it is run
here at its published parameter set and epoch budget, under the same common
optimization setting as the extended baselines. CoWA addresses test-time adaptation rather than this setting, and the difference is not one an extension could absorb: its single streaming pass and its restriction to the normalization parameters are constitutive of the method, so granting it the full target set over repeated epochs would yield a different method. Four representative single-label methods are
therefore extended.
Changes common to all four are: softmax replaced by per-class sigmoids;
categorical cross entropy replaced by binary cross entropy; and the information
maximization diversity term recomputed per class as in
Section 4 . One further change proved necessary twice
independently. Both UCON and NVC-LLN promote prediction dispersion by
minimizing the dot product between the predicted distributions of different
samples in a batch, which is well defined for softmax outputs but degenerate
for independent sigmoids, since that product is minimized trivially by driving
every probability to zero. In both cases the extension L 2 L_{2} -normalizes the sigmoid
vectors before taking the product, penalizing the cosine similarity between
predictions rather than their magnitude. That the same repair is required in
two methods of different lineage is a concrete instance of (P1).

Second, and more consequential for how this problem should be framed, extending
a single-label SFDA method to multi-label data does not reliably beat doing
nothing at all. Two of the four clear the unadapted source model on average,
NVC-LLN by 2.67 2.67 average mAP and AC-SFDA by 1.15 1.15 ; UCON collapses ( − 23.37 -23.37 ), and
SHOT is the clearest case of the pattern: its gains on three tasks and losses
on the other two cancel almost exactly, leaving it level with source-only
( 51.54 51.54 versus 51.54 51.54 ). On two of the five tasks, AID → \rightarrow UCM and
Cityscapes → \rightarrow Foggy, no extended baseline beats source-only at all.
MPACT is the only method that improves on source-only on every task.
The narrowest of those margins is Cityscapes → \rightarrow Foggy, at 0.83 0.83 mAP on average and 0.54 0.54 in the weakest of the three seeds: of the same order
as the seed-to-seed spread, but positive in every seed. Part of
SHOT’s behaviour is structural: its centroid assignment emits a single positive
label per image (Section 5.3 ), yet because evaluation reads the
model’s per-class scores rather than its pseudo-labels, a single-hot training
signal still leaves the ranking usable. The damage surfaces not as uniform
collapse but as unreliability, which is harder to detect and more dangerous in
deployment, since a practitioner cannot tell in advance which side of the ledger
a given domain pair will land on. UCON degrades furthest, reaching 3.04 3.04 F 1 L F_{1}^{L} on VOC → \rightarrow Clipart. Its uncertainty control has no
per-class counterpart and had to be replaced for this study; Appendix A shows that the replacement is not what the collapse rests
on.

Third, two further gaps separate the methods, and neither is visible in

CleanAdapt-TS ( Dasgupta et al., 2025 ) , whose teacher–student scheme this work follows,

pseudo-label is a vector of C C entries of which typically a few are wrong and
the rest are right, so discarding the image discards also some correct entries.

blocks.en:
Two observations make the outcome less surprising. The first is
that the label-level variant is the permissive one: it removes strictly less
supervision than sample-level filtering, so a mechanism that fails here is
unlikely to succeed in its blunter form. The second connects to
Section 6.4 . The filter ranks entries by prototype
similarity, and the diagnostic there shows that on tasks where the source
representation already clusters the target data, most of the agreement between
prototype similarity and the labels is agreement the model has generated
itself. Ranking by that quantity therefore selects for consistency with the
model’s existing beliefs rather than for correctness, and removes precisely the
entries on which the teacher and the prototypes disagree – which is where new
information would have to come from. That the one task with a positive result
is also the one where the diagnostic finds prototype similarity most
informative is consistent with this reading, though with a single seed and one
positive case it is a suggestion rather than a finding.

blocks.en:
The most consequential result of the benchmark is that half of the
extended baselines fail to improve on doing nothing at all. The failures are
not incidental, and the two clearest have separate causes. SHOT’s centroid assignment emits one positive
label per image, so its training signal is single-label regardless. UCON’s
uncertainty control is defined by competition between classes and survives no
per-class substitution, as Appendix A sets out. Neither
mechanism has a multi-label counterpart
that preserves its behaviour, so in both cases what is measured is the
reach of the single-label formulation rather than a deficiency of the
underlying idea.

Two further assumptions break for every method in the comparison rather
than only the baselines: the diversity target of information maximization,
which MPACT inherits in its miscalibrated form and which helps regardless,
and confidence-weighted prototype construction, which MPACT replaces. What
all four have in common is only their origin: each is a place where (P1) or
(P2) was doing silent work, and each fails differently once that is withdrawn.
That is why the setting requires the assumption-by-assumption treatment
attempted here rather than a uniform substitution of sigmoids for softmax.

A second pattern runs through the ablations. The two components that reshape
the target feature space, prototype contrastive alignment and information
maximization, both contribute several times more on VOC → \rightarrow Clipart
than on Clipart → \rightarrow VOC, and the prototype initialization follows the
same ordering. The symmetric term, whose role is to bound the influence of
wrong pseudo-labels rather than to reorganize features, does not. The
asymmetry cannot lie in the domain pair, which is identical in both
directions; it lies in where the source model starts, at 39.77 39.77 mAP on
Clipart against 55.52 55.52 on VOC. Removing prototype contrastive alignment on
VOC → \rightarrow Clipart forfeits 4.70 4.70 of the 5.51 5.51 mAP that adaptation gains
over the source model, against 1.08 1.08 of 7.63 7.63 in the reverse direction. With
two directions this remains just a pattern, but it is the ordering that the
mechanisms claimed in Section 4 predict, and it suggests where to
look: the worse the source model transfers, the larger the share
of the achievable gain that comes from feature-space alignment rather than from
noise robustness. Source-model mAP is a proxy for how far the
representation has to move and not a measure of the domain gap, since a target
set may simply be harder; the pattern is stated for the two directions
examined and not as a law.

Section 6.1 located the remaining deficit in ranking
quality rather than in where the decision boundary falls. That is a more
specific finding than it first appears, because it raises the possibility that
what is hardest to replace without source data is less the raw supervision
than the label marginal. A method
with source access observes how often each class occurs and how classes
co-occur, and inherits a usable prior for both. A source-free method has no
comparable signal, which is why the diversity term of
Section 4 must fall back on a target of q ¯ c = 0.5 \bar{q}_{c}=0.5 that
is wrong for nearly every class in these datasets. A
marginal-aware replacement, in which each class’s diversity target is an
estimate of its frequency, is one route to
narrowing the ranking gap, though no variant of it is tested here. Estimating it from the target data is the difficulty, and prior-correction procedures of the
expectation-maximization family are the natural starting point.

blocks.en:
Several limits of this study should be stated plainly. The ablations are run on
two of the five tasks, and the two VOC ↔ \leftrightarrow Clipart directions were
chosen because they span the worst and one of the best source-to-target
transfers in the benchmark;
whether the component ordering holds on the remote-sensing and driving tasks is
not established here, and the diagnostic of
Section 6.4 adds only one of them. All results use a single backbone, so the comparison
isolates adaptation rather than capacity but says nothing about how the
conclusions scale. Two of the design choices examined in
Section 6.3 are retained for reasons other than
measured performance: the
prototypes are kept static as making them learnable is measurably
neutral, and the classifier head is kept frozen although unfreezing it improves
the two-task average by 0.21 0.21 mAP. Both choices are defensible on terms of comparability, but neither is supported by the measurements, and
presenting them otherwise would misrepresent the evidence. Prototype coverage is incomplete on two tasks: on
VOC → \rightarrow Clipart four of the twenty classes never exceed τ \tau during
initialization and so never receive a prototype, as does one of seventeen on
AID → \rightarrow UCM; the other three tasks cover every class. This is (P2)
acting on the construction itself, and it falls hardest on
VOC → \rightarrow Clipart, the task where the alignment term contributes most. Appendix B shows the cost is nonetheless small: removing the threshold
restores full coverage and loses 1.91 1.91 mAP there, so what the threshold
excludes weighs more than how many anchors it leaves.
The information
maximization term retains the miscalibrated diversity prior discussed above.
Prototype contrastive alignment, the largest contributor in
Section 6.3 , is worth only + 0.86 ± 0.45 +0.86\pm 0.45 mAP averaged over the five
tasks (Table 5 ): it pays on two, is neutral on two and
costs on one. The component ablation is run on the two directions where it
pays, so it overstates what the term contributes benchmark-wide.
The baselines are multi-label extensions constructed for this study rather
than methods published for this setting, so their results characterize how
their mechanisms transfer rather than the performance their authors would
report.

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
This paper formulated source-free domain adaptation for multi-label
classification, identified the specific assumptions of single-label SFDA that
fail in this setting, and proposed MPACT, a mean-teacher framework combining
a symmetric per-class objective, label-similarity weighted prototype
contrastive alignment and multi-label information maximization. By adapting
four single-label SFDA methods to multi-label classification and running
them alongside a published multi-label one, the first
benchmark for this problem was established across five adaptation tasks and six
datasets. On it, MPACT achieves the best average mAP and the best or tied-best mAP on
four of the five tasks, and is the only method to improve on the unadapted source model on
all five; of the four extended baselines, two improve on that model on average,
one ends level with it and one collapses far below it. The accompanying analysis shows that prototype contrastive
alignment contributes unevenly across the five tasks, its largest gain
falling on the transfer where the source model starts weakest, and
introduces a diagnostic for separating genuine alignment from
self-reinforcing agreement – a distinction that should prove useful beyond
this paper. Future work should target the marginal-aware regularization the
multi-label setting demands, and extend the formulation to open and partial
label sets.

What UCON does with those ambiguous pairs instead is itself undefined
here, which is why they are excluded rather than relaxed. Its partial-label
loss supervises precisely the uncertain samples, summing a smoothed cross
entropy over a candidate set of their most probable classes. That is a relaxation only because the candidates compete: exactly one is correct,

every class in the set is present – a stronger claim than the uncertainty
warranted, not a weaker one. By (P1) the construct loses its meaning rather
than its effectiveness, and no per-class reading recovers it.
